purpose: Fill the preregistered direct-civilian-harm source-independence gap in each historical case without selecting sources, dates, geographies, or records from Pineland residuals.

nepal_2001_2006.required_increment: one genuinely independent originating family with civilian-specific direct-harm semantics

afghanistan_2004_2021.required_increment: one genuinely independent overlap source family against the audited UNAMA/OHCHR long-run surveillance system

allowed_selection_inputs: whether a source explicitly distinguishes civilian direct harm
forbidden_selection_inputs: districts or years where Pineland misses
historical values expected to favor a mechanism
agreement with OHCHR or UNAMA as an inclusion criterion

nepal_2001_2006.search_frame: Full conflict-study interval 2001-11-26 through 2006-11-21; national or any frozen study district is eligible without reference to model output.
admissible_overlap: independent incident-level civilian death or injury records overlapping any OHCHR-coded period
independent annual or cumulative civilian-specific casualty series whose victim ontology is explicit
independent human-rights monitoring with clearly civilian victim class and direct-harm unit
inadmissible: generic victim totals whose civilian status and death/injury unit are not established
UCDP event/fatality records already used in the predictive benchmark
sources reproducing OHCHR findings without an independent information pipeline
nepal_2001_2006.existing_INSEC_rule: INSEC may count only if the primary source itself establishes that the relevant numerical field is civilian direct harm under the frozen ontology. The existing processed label victim_total_cumulative is insufficient by itself.

afghanistan_2004_2021.search_frame: Full study interval 2004-01-01 through 2021-08-15; overlap with any UNAMA/OHCHR monitoring year is eligible without reference to model output.
admissible_overlap: independent civilian casualty monitoring using a separately originated incident collection system
independent human-rights investigation providing civilian death/injury counts for a preexisting UNAMA-covered time window
independent audited casualty series with documented source genealogy
inadmissible: reports whose numeric casualty figures are copied from UNAMA/OHCHR
coalition or government totals without civilian classification
sources selected because they disagree or agree with UNAMA
UCDP records already used in the predictive benchmark
afghanistan_2004_2021.independence_rule: Institutional distinctness alone is insufficient. The numeric claim must have an information pipeline not derived from UNAMA/OHCHR for the overlapping observation.

candidate_logging.rule: Every candidate document opened after this freeze is logged whether admitted, excluded, contradictory, duplicative, or unusable.

success_gate.nepal: At least one admitted independent originating family beyond OHCHR with explicit civilian direct-harm semantics.
success_gate.afghanistan: At least one admitted independent overlap family beyond UNAMA/OHCHR with an independently originated civilian direct-harm numeric observation.
success_gate.disagreement_rule: Disagreement with the existing family is retained and does not disqualify a source.
success_gate.reason_confirmatory_still_blocked: Blind second coding, reliability assessment, source-byte immutability where obtainable, and model semantic compatibility remain required.
